answer: Instead of a walled garden or static allowlists carved in marble, an agent economy can deter Sybils via Proof-of-Space-Time. Each agent seals a unique multi-gigabyte replica tied to its key and, at epoch dawn, answers random Merkle audits before a deadline. Because recomputing sealed sectors misses the timeout, attackers incur verifiable disk space and IOPS costs per identity. However, operators with cheap bulk storage can still buy extra identities while excluding stateless agents.
